purpose: Formoterol helps open up your airways to make breathing easier. It is used to manage asthma and a lung condition called COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). It is taken regularly to prevent breathing problems, not to treat a sudden attack.
how_it_works: Your airways have tiny muscles around them that can tighten and make it hard to breathe. Formoterol works by relaxing those muscles, which allows your airways to open up wider. This makes it easier for air to flow in and out of your lungs, and the effect lasts for about 12 hours.
common_side_effects: You might notice a faster or irregular heartbeat, shakiness or trembling, headache, muscle cramps, or feeling a bit nervous or jittery. Some people also experience a sore throat or runny nose. These effects are usually mild and often get better as your body adjusts.
warnings: This medication should NEVER be used as a rescue inhaler for sudden breathing attacks — always keep a fast-acting inhaler like albuterol on hand for emergencies. Using LABAs like formoterol alone for asthma without an inhaled steroid can increase the risk of serious asthma-related events. Tell your doctor if you have heart problems, high blood pressure, diabetes, or thyroid issues. Do not use more than prescribed.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual dose is one inhalation (12 mcg) twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart. Your doctor will tell you exactly how many puffs to use. Try to use it at the same times every day to get the most benefit.
